data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Lebanese army says it seized arms depot in Beirut's southern suburbs
The Lebanese army said on Friday it had raided an arms depot in Beirut's southern suburbs and arrested one person.
The army carried out "a special security operation after close monitoring of the transportation and trade of weapons", targeting an "arms depot in the Msharrafieh area of the southern suburbs", it said in a statement.
It said troops seized a "large number of war arms and munitions", and that the person arrested is under investigation.
The statement did not say who the weapons belonged to.
In June, Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement that included the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual Israeli withdrawal from territory it occupies in the south and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the area.

data.title: Middle East Eye: New Turkey-Qatar pact pledges joint stance against external attacks
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
New Turkey-Qatar pact pledges joint stance against external attacks
Turkey and Qatar have pledged a unified stance against any external armed attack on either country, according to a joint statement issued after they signed the defence agreement.
The statement said the pact aims to strengthen collective defence and promote regional security.
Under it, the two countries will consult on threats to their security, regional and global security issues, and defence policy.
They will also expand cooperation through joint military exercises, defence industry projects and personnel training exchanges.
The statement added that the agreement reflects both countries’ commitment to safeguarding their sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as their shared vision of a more secure and stable regional order.
The two sides also said they were ready to pursue energy cooperation, particularly in liquefied natural gas trade.

data.author: Mounira Elsamra

Submitted by

The airport and New York's Port Authority have come under scrutiny after reports emerged that parts for 'bunker-busting' bombs were going through JFK
People walk through Terminal 7 at JFK Airport in New York City, on 29 August 2025 (Michael M Santiago/Getty Images via AFP)
Off
Activists, joined by New York State Senator Jabari Brisport, gathered outside the World Trade Center on Thursday, protesting against the transportation of military-related materials through JFK International Airport (JFK).
The protest, organised under the “Break the Chain” campaign led by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), comes amid reporting from The Intercept that Challenge Airlines cargo flights have transported materials including nitrocellulose, bomb casings and guidance kits from JFK to Israel.
Open-source data documented in the report reveals weapons flown out of JFK are tied to mass casualty attacks in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran.
Challenge Airlines is an Israel-based cargo airline and logistics company founded in 1976.
The Intercept reported that thousands of pounds worth of parts for "bunker-buster" bombs went through JFK during the height of the US-Israeli war on Iran. The war began on 28 February.
Break the Chain says that military cargo bound for Israel passes through JFK Airport regularly, sometimes multiple times a week, and that civilian infrastructure should not be used for the benefit of the Israeli military.
Protesters, including members of Jewish Voice for Peace, Palestinian Youth Movement, Democratic Socialists of America, and Brooklyn for Peace called for an end to the shipments and greater accountability from the Port Authority, which has jurisdiction over JFK Airport.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Houthis say they attacked Riyadh airport and Saudi oil pipeline
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Houthis say they attacked Riyadh airport and Saudi oil pipeline
Yemen's Houthis said they attacked Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which carries crude oil to the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group targeted the airport with a drone, and a pumping station east of Riyadh with two drones.
The group also fired two ballistic missiles at what Saree described as Saudi troop concentrations in the al-Tuwal area of Jazan, in southern Saudi Arabia, he said.
The group's statements came hours after Saudi civil defence issued an all-clear for the province, which is home to a Saudi Aramco refinery with a capacity of 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day.
Inside Yemen, Saree said the Houthis struck Saudi weapons depots at the Ras Abbas camp in Aden with ballistic missiles and drones.
He added that they also fired missiles at forces under the command of Saudi officers in Lahj and al-Jawf provinces, claiming they caused many casualties.
Saudi Arabia did not immediately confirm the Houthi claims.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli forces detain Palestinian groom in wedding raid as settler attacks continue across West Bank
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Israeli forces detain Palestinian groom in wedding raid as settler attacks continue across West Bank
Israeli forces and settlers carried out a series of attacks across the occupied West Bank on Friday, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.
In Jaba’, south of Jenin, Israeli forces stormed the town, firing live ammunition and tear gas, and shot a young Palestinian man in the thigh, the Palestinian Red Crescent Society said.
Near Ramallah, Israeli forces raided a wedding hall in the village of al-Mughayyir, firing tear gas at around 150 guests and detaining four people, including the groom, Wafa said, citing Palestinian residents.
In the same village, troops stormed the home of Palestinian man, Hamed Abu Naim, seized keys and forced the family out.
In Beit Ummar, north of Hebron, several Palestinians were treated for tear gas inhalation after Israeli forces fired tear gas at residents and their homes.
According to residents, troops had entered the town to protect Israeli settlers who had chased children near its entrance and tried to assault them. Soldiers also stopped a vehicle at the entrance and beat its driver.
South of Yatta, in the Hebron governorate, settlers besieged the home of Yousef Shannaran for the 40th consecutive day, media activist Osama Makhamra told Wafa.
He said settlers had put back up a tent next to the house that Israeli forces had previously removed, so the family can only come and go by coordinating with nearby troops. Settlers also threw stones at the home, smashed its windows and doors and poisoned the family’s water well, he added.
Near Khirbet Srouj, west of Jenin, settlers attacked Palestinian families harvesting olives and stole harvested olives and equipment.
In occupied East Jerusalem, two Palestinian brothers were forced to demolish their own homes in Sur Baher after the Israeli municipality said they had been built without permits.
Israeli forces also detained a Palestinian child and a woman in the southern Hebron area, Quds News

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise
US President Donald Trump has extended by 90 days a waiver of a shipping law so that foreign-flagged ships can transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday.
The administration would extend the waiver of the more than 100-year-old Jones Act, Reuters reported, citing industry sources.
The administration issued a blanket waiver in March, a month after the US launched its war on Iran, in an effort to lower oil and fuel prices.
When it extended the waiver in August, it said it would decide cases on a case-by-case basis, a condition that also applies to the latest extension.
The Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies, and crewed by American workers. The waiver aims to lower gasoline, diesel, and fertiliser prices, which have risen because of the war.
Since March, an additional 90 million barrels of petroleum, mostly refined products, have been shipped between US ports under the waiver, the White House said.

data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Six Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza
Israeli attacks killed six Palestinians and injured around 20 others across the Gaza Strip on Friday, according to medical sources and witnesses.
In Deir al-Balah, a double-tap strike hit civilians who were helping victims of an earlier attack, witnesses said.
Israeli artillery shelled the area around the al-Qastal Towers residential complex, east of the city, Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. Those wounded were taken to al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah.
Israeli artillery also shelled eastern areas of Gaza City, Wafa added.
Since the ceasefire took effect on 11 October 2025, Israeli attacks have killed 1,622 Palestinians and injured 5,878 others, according to Gaza's health ministry.

data.title: Middle East Eye: US responds to suspected drone activity over UK air base used in Iran strikes
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
US responds to suspected drone activity over UK air base used in Iran strikes
US Air Force personnel at the RAF Lakenheath base in Britain responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” on Friday evening, a US Air Force spokesperson said, adding that no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected.
“We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families,” the spokesperson said by email.
Britain's Ministry of Defence said US Air Force Security Forces personnel had responded to reports of unauthorised drone activity and that the situation had been resolved.
In recent weeks, the US has moved bombers that had been used to strike Iran out of Britain, and relocated large refuelling aircraft from Britain to Germany. The Wall Street Journal reported that the moves were due to a threat from Iran.
The bombers left RAF Fairford on security grounds after a group of men approached the base in white vans on the night of 27 September.
Two men were charged last month in relation to that incident, with prosecutors alleging that one of them had tried to assist Iranian intelligence in Britain.
The US Justice Department said this week that a member of an Iran-backed militia had plotted to attack the Fairford base while detained in the US on criminal charges.
Tehran has denied involvement in the Fairford incident and rejected other accusations of malign activity in Britain.

data.title: Middle East Eye: US flights halted nationwide after FAA communications outage
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
US flights halted nationwide after FAA communications outage
The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered a nationwide ground stop following a telecommunications outage affecting air traffic control operations, suspending departures across the country. Flights already airborne have been allowed to continue to their destinations while authorities work to resolve the disruption.
More than 10,000 flights were delayed and over 2,000 cancelled, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware, with CBS News reporting that a software update to a private communications network connecting air traffic control facilities across the US caused the system to reboot and crash, triggering the outage.
The nationwide ground stop is the first since January 2023, when an FAA computer system malfunction disrupted operations. The previous major halt followed the September 11, 2001 attacks.
Flight-tracking service Flightradar24 reported just 1,000 flights heading to US airports, down nearly 80 percent from more than 4,500 a week earlier.
* JetBlue Airways reported departure delays, saying it was monitoring developments and would resume operations once authorities permitted flights to take off.
* Air Canada warned that flights to and from the Caribbean and South America could be affected, advising passengers to check its app for updates.
* Britain's Civil Aviation Authority warned travellers of disruption to flights to, from and within the US, urging passengers to check with airlines.

data.title: Middle East Eye: UN, partners urge Israel to lift restrictions on aid into Gaza
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
UN, partners urge Israel to lift restrictions on aid into Gaza
The UN and its humanitarian partners have called on Israel to lift restrictions on aid deliveries to Gaza, warning that deadly rainstorms have killed children and adults, destroyed shelters and flooded thousands of family tents.
More than 150,000 tents remain outside Gaza, ready for dispatch, as restrictions on supplies and access continue to hamper winter preparations, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).
In a statement, the Humanitarian Country Team, comprising UN agencies and humanitarian organisations operating in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, said the devastation caused by the rainstorms was preventable.
Humanitarian partners had presented a winter preparedness plan months ago, but restrictions on supplies and access, alongside funding shortfalls, had hampered its implementation.
The Team urged Israel to lift restrictions, enable repairs to water and wastewater networks, and allow all humanitarian partners to operate.
The appeal follows a statement earlier this week by Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher, who warned that delays, restrictions and funding cuts were putting lives at risk.
The Humanitarian Country Team also urged member states to use their influence to remove obstacles to aid deliveries and provide urgently needed funding.

Rubio says economic pain inflicted on Iran makes military action unnecessary
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said that further US military action against Iran is unnecessary because the economic pain the Washington is inflicting on a "weakened" Tehran "is so great".
“And right now, frankly, the economic pain that we are inflicting on that regime is so great that there’s no need for military action because we’ve weakened them so much,” Rubio said in his address to the Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention in Washington.
“But I think victory is ensuring that they never have a nuclear weapon,” he added.
At the same time, Rubio acknowledge the economic pain Americans have experienced as a result of the war, which has driven up fuel costs and affected nearly every sector of the global economy.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran warns of 'immediate response' to any US-Israeli attack, slams Gulf nations
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Iran warns of 'immediate response' to any US-Israeli attack, slams Gulf nations
Iran has said that any renewed US-Israeli attacks on its territory would trigger an immediate response, while accusing Bahrain and other Gulf countries of facilitating Washington’s military operations against Tehran.
“Any renewed war of aggression by the United States and the Israeli regime will be met with an immediate and decisive response, without hesitation,” said Gholamhossein Darzi, Iran's deputy permanent representative to the UN, during a Security Council meeting on the situation in the Middle East.
"We regret the positions taken by some Council members, particularly its Western members. Their statements reflect a familiar pattern of double standards and blatant hypocrisy," he told the council.
He also accused some Gulf countries of allowing their territory, airspace and military facilities to be used for US-Israeli attacks, arguing that they should be held accountable and compensate Iran for the resulting damage.
In a subsequent exchange with Bahrain’s representative, Darzi singled out the kingdom, saying it had facilitated US military operations against Tehran.
Bahrain rejected Iran’s accusations and said Tehran could not invoke its right to self-defence to justify attacks on neighbouring countries.
Darzi demanded that Washington end its military operations, lift its blockade and provide guarantees against further strikes.

Rubio targets ICC: 'Won't submit to sterile vision of radical judges':
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has attacked the International Criminal Court (ICC) in a speech to a conservative legal group on Friday, arguing for a muscular foreign policy and against international law restraining US actions.
During his speech to the Federalist Society in Washington, his first prepared remarks since Republicans were routed in the midterm elections on 3 November, Rubio said the goal of the US-Israeli war against Iran was to prevent Tehran from ever developing a nuclear weapon, which he said was particularly urgent because the Islamic Republic's "radical Shia clerics" had an "expansionist mentality."
He contrasted this with the government of North Korea's Kim Jong Un, whom Trump has met three times. "I'm not excusing the terrible things that have happened there," Rubio said of North Korea. "I'm just saying he (Kim) is not expansionist. He's not trying to invade Japan or, you know, China or whatever."
Rubio dismissed criticisms that the Trump administration has broken international law by such actions as seizing Venezuelan then-President Nicolas Maduro and striking boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific that it says were carrying drugs.
The US, Rubio said, would not “submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats,” repeating his assertion that the court would try to prosecute US officials or service members that he used to justify sanctions against the ICC announced last month.
“Americans have never agreed to submit to the ICC's authority, but that court and its allies in the global bureaucracy have appointed themselves judge and jury and executioner of the international order,” Rubio said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump to discuss Iran war, but not Ukraine, at China summit
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Trump to discuss Iran war, but not Ukraine, at China summit
US President Donald Trump will discuss the Iran war with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week but he is not expected to discuss Ukraine war, a US official said.
The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.
"The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous," Wales said.
"I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin," a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.
Washington has a "whole other track" of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
"China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn't seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there," the official added.
Report by AFP

data.title: Middle East Eye: UN says IMO confirms 25 seafarer deaths since Iran war began
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
UN says IMO confirms 25 seafarer deaths since Iran war began
As many as 25 seafarers have been killed in 134 confirmed maritime incidents across the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Middle East since the US and Israeli started war on Iran in February, according to Khalid Khiari, UN Assistant Secretary-General Khaled for the Middle East, Asia and the Pacific.
Briefing the UN Security Council on Friday, Khiari cited figures from the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) covering incidents recorded up to November 11.
He said October saw the highest monthly number of incidents involving commercial shipping since February, warning that continued disruption was driving up energy, transport and insurance costs and threatening global food security.
“This situation cannot be allowed to become the new normal,” Khiari said, calling for an immediate end to attacks on civilian vessels and the restoration of safe maritime navigation.
Bahrain’s representative told the meeting that about 1,600 vessels had been affected by disruptions in the waterway, leaving more than 23,000 seafarers stranded aboard their ships.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Mossad chief in Washington for talks on Iran, report says
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Mossad chief in Washington for talks on Iran, report says
Roman Gofman, chief of Israeli spy agency Mossad and one of Benjamin Netanyahu's closest confidants, was in Washington on Friday for talks with senior Trump administration officials about the war in Iran, Axios reported, citing three sources with knowledge of the matter.
The visit comes as the Israeli prime minister is pressing President Trump to resume the war against Iran. Axios said Gofman was to meet CIA Director John Ratcliffe and later expected to travel to Miami to meet White House envoy Steve Witkoff.
Mossad, the CIA and the White House declined to comment, Axios said.
Meanwhile Israel's Channel 12 news reported that Gofman’s trip was not disclosed to Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot in his Thursday security briefing with Netanyahu.
Trump, who suffered a defeat in the midterm elections, has resisted the pressure to resume strikes on Iran. Also, on Friday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that further military action against Iran was unnecessary because the "economic pain" inflicted by the US sanctions on Tehran "was so great".
